approvalRequirements: Be an Enbridge Gas Utah commercial customer with an active meter on an eligible general service rate.
Purchase and install new equipment or measures that meet the current ThermWise business specifications.
Submit the applicable signed rebate form and required proof of purchase and installation after completion.
Complete any verification requested by Enbridge Gas.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a current prescriptive rebate pathway with objective customer, equipment and documentation criteria. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current ThermWise business page requires an active general-service meter, installation of a qualified measure, and a signed rebate application with supporting documents.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Dominion Energy South Carolina non-residential electric customer.
Submit the measure-specific application and worksheet and obtain written pre-approval before purchasing or installing equipment.
Install the approved qualifying equipment within the authorized project period.
Submit final approval documents, invoices and proof of installation, and permit inspection if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program uses a defined pre-approval and final-claim process. Projects that reserve eligibility, install approved measures and submit complete closeout evidence are likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Current business incentive pages direct customers to apply for pre-approval before purchase, then submit installation evidence for final approval and payment.

approvalRequirements: Construct an eligible residential property served by Enbridge Gas in Utah.
Install qualifying high-efficiency gas equipment or meet an eligible whole-home standard.
Submit the applicable builder application, worksheet, IRS Form W-9 and supporting documents.
Postmark or submit the request within six months of Enbridge Gas service turn-on; coordinate with the program for multifamily projects.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current builder program states clear equipment, documentation and timing requirements. A conforming submission is likely to be awarded after review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current builder page requires qualifying construction, application materials and supporting documents, with requests due within six months of service turn-on.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Enbridge Gas residential customer in Utah.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying appliance, HVAC or weatherization measure that meets published specifications.
Use a ThermWise authorized contractor for air sealing, duct work and other measures where required; obtain multifamily pre-qualification inspection where applicable.
Submit the applicable rebate application and supporting purchase and installation documents.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The active program provides prescriptive rebates under published specifications. Eligible completed measures with the required contractor, inspection and documentation are likely to be paid.
reviews.evidenceText: Current ThermWise pages list qualifying residential equipment and weatherization measures, application routes, authorized-contractor rules and multifamily pre-inspection requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Enbridge Gas residential customer in Utah.
Install a qualifying solar-assisted gas water-heating system; the whole system must have current SRCC OG-300 certification.
Complete the solar-specific rebate application and submit required purchase and installation documentation.
Satisfy any program verification request.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current appliance schedule expressly lists a rebate for an SRCC-certified solar-assisted gas water-heating system. A complete claim meeting those objective specifications is likely to be awarded.
reviews.evidenceText: The current appliance page lists solar-assisted gas water heating as eligible only for an SRCC OG-300 whole system and requires a solar application.

Submit the applicable signed Utah/Idaho rebate form and required proof of purchase and installation after completion.

reviews.evidenceText: The current ThermWise business page covers Utah and Idaho forms and requires an active general-service meter, a qualified installed measure, a signed application and supporting documents.

approvalRequirements: Construct an eligible residential property served by Enbridge Gas in Idaho.
Install qualifying high-efficiency gas equipment or meet an eligible whole-home standard.
Submit the applicable Utah/Idaho builder application, worksheet, IRS Form W-9 and supporting documents.

Use a ThermWise authorized contractor for air sealing, duct work and other measures where required; obtain multifamily pre-qualification inspection where applicable.
Submit the applicable Utah/Idaho rebate application and supporting purchase and installation documents.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Dominion Energy South Carolina residential electric customer.
Replace existing equipment with a qualifying high-efficiency unit meeting the current ENERGY STAR or AHRI requirements.
Use an appropriately licensed contractor where the measure requires professional installation.
Submit the completed rebate application and itemized invoice within the stated post-installation deadline, generally 90 days for listed HVAC and water-heating rebates.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential pages use objective customer, equipment, contractor and filing criteria. A timely complete application for a listed measure is likely to receive the rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current South Carolina residential pages require qualifying replacement equipment, contractor installation where applicable, and a complete application with invoice after installation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Enbridge Gas North Carolina business customer.
Purchase qualifying new business equipment that meets the current efficiency requirements.
Have the equipment installed by a licensed contractor.
Submit the correct rebate form and itemized receipt within 90 days of installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Enbridge Gas business program provides a defined bill-credit process. Eligible equipment installed by a licensed contractor and documented within 90 days is likely to be approved.
reviews.evidenceText: The current North Carolina business page requires a completed equipment or food-service form, licensed-contractor installation and an itemized receipt submitted within 90 days.

approvalRequirements: Be a current Dominion Energy Virginia residential customer in an eligible residence and rate class.
Purchase and install a currently qualified connected Level 2 charger and register it with the manufacturer.
Enroll in EV Charger Rewards, accept managed-charging terms and provide the required account, charger and purchase information.
Receive program acceptance before an enrollment rebate or recurring reward is issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: A current Dominion Energy page confirms that EV Charger Rewards provides rebates for a new qualified charger registered with its manufacturer. The detailed official enrollment article is older, so current model, rate and payment terms should be reconfirmed before purchase.
reviews.evidenceText: The current 2026 Dominion page confirms the rebate program and manufacturer-registration requirement. An older official detailed page states that program acceptance is required after enrollment.

approvalRequirements: Be a Dominion Energy Virginia customer responsible for the electric bill on an eligible non-residential rate.
Own the facility or have authority to install the measures and not be excluded by statute or special contract.
Use a participating contractor or program representative and reserve rebate funding before installation where the selected pathway requires it.
Install qualifying measures and have the contractor submit a complete rebate packet.
Pass any required inspection or final savings verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current business programs use participating contractors, documented eligibility and final verification. A project with reserved funding that completes the approved scope and rebate packet is likely to receive payment.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Dominion-linked business pages require an eligible Virginia non-residential account, contractor assessment or reservation, qualifying installation and a final rebate packet, with inspection or verification where applicable.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Dominion Energy Virginia residential customer.
Select a participating contractor and complete the required Home Energy Evaluation.
Choose and complete eligible improvements recommended or accepted through the program.
Have the participating contractor submit the rebate application and supporting project information after the work is completed.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Home Energy Evaluation pathway has a defined contractor-led process. Completed eligible improvements with a contractor-submitted application are likely to receive the applicable rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Home Energy Evaluation page directs customers to a participating contractor, an evaluation, selected improvements and a contractor-submitted rebate application after completion.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Douglas Electric Cooperative member at the installation site.
Obtain pre-approval before installation for measures whose current page requires it, including ductless heat pumps.
Install equipment or envelope measures meeting the current Bonneville Power Administration and cooperative specifications.
Submit the current application, invoices or receipts and required photos or pre-existing-condition evidence.
Complete any installation verification requested by the cooperative or program implementer.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative publishes current measure-specific criteria and a rebate process. A member who secures required pre-approval and submits complete evidence for qualifying work is likely to receive the rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current cooperative pages state that ductless heat pumps require pre-approval, insulation claims need proof of the original R-value, and qualifying heat-pump water heaters are subject to measure-specific limits.

approvalRequirements: Be a current DTE Electric residential customer with an account in good standing.
Meet the current household-income eligibility requirement or qualify through an accepted energy-assistance verification route.
Purchase or lease an eligible EV or plug-in hybrid and install a qualifying new Level 2 charger.
Submit the rebate application within six months of charger installation with required vehicle, charger, installation and income-verification information.
Receive DTE application approval.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current DTE program states that a rebate is issued when the published customer, income, vehicle, charger and filing requirements are met and the application is approved.
reviews.evidenceText: The 2026 DTE page requires an eligible electric residential account, income qualification, a qualifying Level 2 charger and an application within six months; approved applicants receive a rebate check.

approvalRequirements: Be a DTE Electric commercial or industrial customer in good standing at a DTE-served facility.
Select equipment or a project that meets the current 2026 catalog requirements.
Obtain a project reservation before purchase or installation where required; reservation is strongly encouraged for other projects.
Complete the project within the reservation or program deadline and submit the final application with invoices, specification sheets, agreements and signatures.
Pass any required pre-inspection, post-inspection or final technical review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program is a current, rules-based incentive offering. Reserved or otherwise eligible projects that satisfy the catalog and complete final review are likely to be paid, although awards remain subject to available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The current 2026 catalog and policies require an eligible DTE facility, qualifying equipment, reservation for specified projects, timely completion and a complete final application; final review and inspection may apply.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible DTE Electric residential customer at a qualifying existing single-family home.
Purchase or install a currently listed qualifying replacement measure or appliance meeting the published efficiency specifications.
Use a DTE participating contractor for HVAC measures; the contractor submits the HVAC rebate form.
For customer-submitted measures, file the online claim with the original receipt and product details within the stated deadline, generally within six months and no later than December 31, 2026.
Apply while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current DTE pages provide objective requirements and direct submission routes. A qualifying, timely and complete claim is likely to be paid while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Current 2026 DTE pages confirm contractor-submitted HVAC rebates and post-purchase claims for qualifying insulation and laundry equipment, with receipts, deadlines and limited funds.

approvalRequirements: Be a DTE Gas commercial or industrial customer in good standing at a DTE-served facility.
Select equipment or a project that meets the current 2026 gas-program catalog requirements.
Obtain a project reservation before purchase or installation where required; reservation is strongly encouraged for other projects.
Complete the project within the reservation or program deadline and submit the final application with invoices, specification sheets, agreements and signatures.
Pass any required pre-inspection, post-inspection or final technical review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program is a current, rules-based incentive offering. Reserved or otherwise eligible gas projects that satisfy the catalog and complete final review are likely to be paid, although awards remain subject to available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The current 2026 catalog and policies require an eligible DTE facility, qualifying gas-saving equipment, reservation for specified projects, timely completion and a complete final application; final review and inspection may apply.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible DTE natural-gas residential customer at a qualifying existing single-family home.
Purchase or install a currently listed qualifying furnace, thermostat, insulation or laundry measure meeting published specifications.
Use a DTE participating contractor for contractor-delivered heating measures; the contractor submits the applicable rebate form.
For customer-submitted measures, provide the original receipt and product information within the stated deadline, generally within six months and no later than December 31, 2026.
Apply while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current DTE pages provide objective gas-customer, equipment and filing requirements. A qualifying, timely and complete claim is likely to be paid while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Current 2026 DTE pages confirm participating-contractor heating rebates and post-purchase thermostat, insulation and laundry claims, with product rules, receipts, deadlines and limited funds.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Duke Energy Kentucky residential customer.
Install a currently qualifying replacement or home-efficiency measure that meets the applicable program specifications.
Use a Duke Energy participating contractor where required for the selected measure.
Have the contractor complete and submit the rebate application and required installation documentation.
Receive Duke Energy approval of the completed claim.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Smart $aver pathway is contractor-led and uses published measure requirements. A qualifying installation with a complete contractor submission is likely to be approved and paid.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Duke pages direct customers to qualifying projects and participating contractors; the contractor completes the rebate application, and approved claims are paid after review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Duke Energy Indiana non-residential customer.
Select equipment that meets the current Smart $aver prescriptive or custom eligibility requirements.
Submit the required online or paper application and supporting technical information; obtain pre-qualification before installation where the project pathway requires it.
Complete the approved installation and provide invoices and final supporting documentation within the applicable authorization period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Smart $aver is a current application-based rebate program with published eligibility and documentation requirements. A qualifying project that follows any required pre-qualification and final submission steps is likely to receive the rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Duke business pages provide Indiana applications and equipment offers; the Smart $aver team reviews applications and issues time-limited pre-qualification where applicable.

approvalRequirements: Be a Duke Energy North Carolina residential customer at an eligible property.
Complete the program eligibility form.
Complete the free home energy audit with a Duke Energy advisor.
Receive and accept an approved improvement plan for measures that meet the program energy-savings and property requirements.
Use the designated installation process and accept the approved on-bill repayment terms.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program is active, but financing is offered only after the property and proposed improvements pass eligibility and audit review. An applicant cannot assume an award before the approved plan is issued.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Improve & Save page starts with an eligibility form and free audit, then provides an improvement plan before upgrades and on-bill repayment begin.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Duke Energy Kentucky non-residential customer.
Select lighting, refrigeration, compressed-air or other equipment that meets the current Smart $aver requirements.
Submit the required online or paper application and supporting technical information; obtain pre-qualification before installation where the project pathway requires it.
Complete the approved installation and provide invoices and final supporting documentation within the applicable authorization period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Smart $aver is a current application-based rebate program with published Kentucky forms and equipment categories. A qualifying project that follows any required pre-qualification and final submission steps is likely to receive the rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Duke business pages provide Kentucky applications and prescriptive offers for lighting and industrial equipment; the Smart $aver team reviews applications and issues pre-qualification where applicable.

approvalRequirements: No current application requirements are available because the Park & Plug pilot has been completed.
Historically, prospective Florida host sites applied and were selected for charger installation through the pilot.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Duke Energy officially announced completion of the Park & Plug pilot in 2022 after the planned charging network was installed. The current informational page does not provide a new host-site award application.
reviews.evidenceText: Official Duke sources describe Park & Plug as a completed Florida pilot with installed charging ports, not an open rebate or site-host application program.

approvalRequirements: Be a North Carolina homeowner and residential customer of Duke Energy Carolinas or Duke Energy Progress.
Install new qualifying solar generation and battery storage together using a Duke Energy Trade Ally and approved equipment.
Meet Duke Energy interconnection requirements and enroll on an eligible residential solar or net-metering rider.
Submit a PowerPair application for system-eligibility and available-capacity review; accept waitlist placement if capacity is unavailable.
Maintain required internet connectivity, data access and battery-control participation where applicable under the selected option.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PowerPair is current, but enrollment is first-come, first-served and each application is reviewed for both system eligibility and remaining program capacity. A technically eligible project may be waitlisted rather than awarded immediately.
reviews.evidenceText: The current PowerPair page requires a qualifying paired solar-and-battery system, a Duke Trade Ally and application review for available capacity. It does not establish eligibility for window replacement or standalone submetering.
